objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a young adult patient presenting with altered mental status, suspected of having a serious drug reaction.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’m not going to answer questions.
I understand you may not feel like talking right now, but I need to make sure you're safe. Are you currently experiencing any pain or discomfort?
I’m too drowsy to respond and I feel unwell. I’ve had a very high fever, my heart’s racing, and my muscles feel rigid.
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed any medications, particularly antipsychotics, antidepressants, anti-nausea drugs, or anything given during a recent surgery or procedure?

Doctor: Have you recently started, stopped, or changed any medications, particularly antipsychotics, antidepressants, anti-nausea drugs, or anything given during a recent surgery or procedure? Patient: I don’t know—I can’t think straight. I’ve taken substances recently, and now I have a very high fever, my heart is racing, and my muscles are rigid.
Along with the stiffness, are you experiencing any involuntary muscle twitching, tremors, or jerking movements, particularly in your legs or feet?

Doctor: Along with the stiffness, are you experiencing any involuntary muscle twitching, tremors, or jerking movements, particularly in your legs or feet? Patient: I’m not able to tell—my body feels rigid and I’m very drowsy, but I don’t feel like I can control my movements.
Is your skin heavily sweating, or is it dry and hot to the touch?
My skin feels hot but not like I’m sweating a lot—more dry, with dry mouth. I’m very drowsy and can’t stay alert enough to move normally.
Are your pupils noticeably dilated (very large), or do they appear normal in size?
Patient: My eyes feel like they’re not focusing right, but I don’t know if my pupils are dilated or not—I can’t really tell. I’m too drowsy and my body feels rigid and unwell.
Do you have any rhythmic, involuntary jerking or shaking in your legs or feet?

Doctor: Do you have any rhythmic, involuntary jerking or shaking in your legs or feet? Patient: I can’t really tell—I just feel very rigid and extremely drowsy, and I don’t feel able to control or notice my movements.
[DDX] Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, Anticholinergic Toxicity, Serotonin Syndrome, Malignant Hyperthermia, Sympathomimetic Intoxication
